To reuse the cockpit for a new project, replace this file (+ GOALS.md). `goals` is auto-filled from GOALS.md by build_portal_data.mjs — do not hand-edit it here. Page `blocks` use a fixed block-type vocabulary (hero, callout, secTitle, statGrid, goals, cardGrid, flow, table, modelList, trace, html). Dynamic pages (no `blocks`) keep their UI shell in index.html and only take kicker/title/lead from here.

blocks.titleHtml: Install a package, build your own agent — in two hours.
blocks.bodyHtml: An Agentforce package customers install into their own sandbox — it lands the permission sets, the ready-made actions, a Lightning app, and a starter Employee Agent V1 (a meeting-note agent). A self-guided web app then walks a non-developer through building and testing that agent in Agent Studio. From "installed" to "a working agent they made" inside a hands-on workshop.

Ship two things that work together: (1) an installable Salesforce package (install link — not a scary browser-OAuth flow) that lands the permission sets, the action assets, a Lightning app, and the Employee Agent V1 starter; and (2) a self-guided React web app that takes a non-expert from get an org → install → build the agent in Agent Studio (instructions + actions) → preview → commit → test, with org sign-up and a free backup org so nobody gets stuck. The agent itself is built in-org because AiAuthoringBundle can't be packaged.

blocks.text: How it will work, in one breath

cards.bodyHtml: The customer installs our package (an install link) into their sandbox. It lands the perm sets, action assets, a Lightning app, and the Employee Agent V1 starter — no Setup spelunking, no CLI.
Guided by the web app, the attendee writes reasoning instructions and adds the Note + Summarize actions from the asset library — then previews and commits the agent live.
They test it (notes → summarize → log to a record), then in the free exercise add Query Records, draft email, Search Web and more — all inside the two-hour session.

pages.titleHtml: How it works — install once, deploy at runtime
pages.leadHtml: Decided: distribute the supporting assets as an installable package (install link) — not a browser-OAuth flow that triggers security warnings. The package can't carry the agent itself (Agent Script AiAuthoringBundle isn't packageable), so it ships everything around the agent — permission sets, the action assets, a Lightning app, and a starter template — and the attendee builds the agent in Agent Studio during the workshop.

cards.bodyHtml: An install link, not a custom browser-OAuth deploy — chosen specifically to avoid the security warnings and participant anxiety that path causes. Reliable, consistent environment for every attendee.

Because AiAuthoringBundle can't be packaged, the package carries the perm sets + action assets + Lightning app + starter template; the agent is built in-org in Agent Studio. (Stretch: a one-click in-org deploy accelerator — secondary.)

The agent's actions — Log/Create Note (Flow), Summarize (Prompt Template), plus Query Records / Search Web / draft email — favor standard/OOB actions. Custom Apex only where it earns its keep (HTML notes, SOSL search).
Flaky Wi-Fi, provisioning hiccups, mixed skill levels — so a free, pre-configured backup org is on hand for anyone whose own org won't cooperate. No dead-ends.

blocks.bodyHtml: Which Agentforce metadata is packageable vs needs prework; managed vs unlocked 2GP for the install link; exactly how perms get assigned on install; and whether a one-click in-org agent-deploy accelerator is worth adding. See Build Tasks + Research Rounds.

pages.leadHtml: During the hackathon day, customers spend two hours building Employee Agent V1 — a meeting-note agent — in their own sandbox, guided by the self-guided web app. The flow is decided: a guided MVP build (Part A), then a free improvement exercise (Part B).

blocks.titleHtml: 🎓 The use case — Employee Agent V1
blocks.bodyHtml: A conversational agent that accepts notes or meeting transcripts (text / upload / voice) and turns them into action: logs them to a Notes record, summarizes, creates follow-up tasks, and drafts a follow-up email. Universally relevant — the simplest way to grasp agent · instructions · actions before connecting more complex use cases.

blocks.titleHtml: ✅ What's preconfigured (so the 2 hours are spent building, not setting up)
blocks.bodyHtml: Foundations access; permission sets assigned (Prompt Template User, Agentforce User, …); the action assets (Flow/Apex/prompt templates) in the asset library; and the Employee Agent V1 starter framework. All delivered by the installable package (+ light prework).

nodes.title: Check the basics
nodes.body: Open Employee Agent V1 in Agent Studio; review details, system & language settings.

nodes.title: Reasoning instructions
nodes.body: Write the natural-language guidance: take unstructured notes → research → store to a Notes record, associate to the current record.

nodes.title: Add actions
nodes.body: From the asset library: Log/Create Note (Flow) + Summarize (Prompt Template). Only the actions it needs.

nodes.title: Preview
nodes.body: Live-test the conversation end-to-end; watch the reasoning + which actions fire.

nodes.title: Commit version
nodes.body: Save & commit → the agent goes live and its icon appears in the app (perms already assigned).

nodes.title: Test on a record
nodes.body: Ask for notes → it validates the record, summarizes, and logs the notes.

cards.bodyHtml: Add the draft-email action; play with format and tone to fit the attendee's business.
Auto-extract call-to-actions into to-do tasks — input to action with no manual work.
Find an account/case to associate the notes to; enrich the transcript with web info or Knowledge.
Enrich the input options (LWC); plus any custom action the attendee dreams up.

blocks.titleHtml: 🚨 The thing that must not happen
blocks.bodyHtml: An attendee stuck on a dead-end (org won't provision, perms missing) with no way forward. The safety nets: the free pre-configured backup org, package-based install (no scary browser-OAuth warnings), and perms assigned up front. "Robust to the room" is a hard constraint, not a nicety.

pages.leadHtml: The thing customers install. An SFDX project (this repo) that packages a Lightning Home app, a runtime agent-deploy LWC + its Apex, the permission sets / groups, and a library of template agents. Built with the pre-installed Agentforce DX skills under .agents/skills/.

cards.bodyHtml: The perms that authorize the attendee (Prompt Template User, Agentforce User, agent-user perms) — assigned on install / prework, no manual Setup. Model on the scaffold's Resort_Agent/Resort_Admin + AFDX_* groups. scaffolded

The Flow/Apex/prompt templates the agent uses — Log/Create Note (Flow), Summarize (Prompt Template), plus Query Records / draft email / Search Web for the free exercise. Loaded into the asset library so attendees just add them. planned
The surface the install lands in, where the attendee finds Agent Studio + their committed agent's icon. planned
The starter agent template attendees build on. The repo already ships Note_taking_agent (the V1 use case) + Local_Info_Agent as references. scaffolded

blocks.bodyHtml: Because AiAuthoringBundle can't be packaged, the agent is normally built in Agent Studio during the workshop. An optional accelerator — a component that deploys the agent in-org at runtime (Metadata/Tooling API) — is a secondary nice-to-have, not the primary path.

blocks.titleHtml: 🛠️ Build it with the installed skills
blocks.bodyHtml: .agents/skills/ ships developing-agentforce, generating-lwc-components, generating-permission-set, generating-apex, deploying-metadata, and testing-agentforce. Use them for the real Salesforce work rather than reinventing the conventions.

cards.bodyHtml: A linear, verifiable flow: get an org → install the package → Part A guided build (instructions → actions → preview → commit → test) → Part B free exercise. Each step shows progress.

A free, pre-configured org for anyone whose primary org fails — the room's safety net, handed over without derailing the session.
Keep the polished Vite/React shell + Heroku deploy; replace the content (it currently guides a different, vibe-coding workshop). Re-script per web-app/CLAUDE.md.

pages.leadHtml: The starter attendees build on. One clear, working agent — the meeting-note agent — simple enough to configure inside the two-hour window, useful enough to feel real.

blocks.titleHtml: 🤖 Employee Agent V1 — the meeting-note agent
blocks.bodyHtml: Already seeded in force-app/ as Note_taking_agent (template EmployeeCopilot__AgentforceEmployeeAgent). It takes unstructured notes/transcripts and logs them to a Notes record (via the First_Agent_Log_Account_Note Flow), associating to the current record. The workshop has attendees add the Summarize action, then extend it (draft email, Query Records, tasks, web search) in the free exercise.

The repo also ships Local_Info_Agent — a resort copilot showing three subagent types (Invocable Apex, Prompt Template, Flow), mutable variables, and deterministic if/else routing. A handy reference for the action patterns, not the workshop's focus.

The exact starter state for the workshop (the planning doc favors starting from a template with no actions so attendees add them), the final reasoning-instruction wording (kept simple — non-coding), and whether we pre-create the agent framework or have attendees create it. Tracked in Build Tasks.

pages.leadHtml: Open questions get answered in rounds — fact-checked investigations (e.g. the exact runtime-deploy API for an AiAuthoringBundle, the perm-set-assignment surface, package type). Each round has status, dates, an outcome, and the agent sessions that produced it.
The package and the web app, built as discrete tasks — each with status, dates, outcome and its associated agent sessions. This is how both flavors get built, step by step.
Every meaningful step, dated. This is the self-evolving spine of the report — it mirrors the agent-facing PROGRESS.md (and is generated from it). Newest first.

Every document this workspace produces — Markdown notes, specs and reports, plus generated HTML reports & decks — in one browsable explorer. Markdown renders inline; HTML opens live. Auto-discovered on each build (scripts/build_portal_data.mjs) — drop a new .md/.html and it appears here, no portal edits.

Every AI session on this project — captured automatically by a Stop hook each turn. Pick a session to read its summary and the full conversation & tool calls. Sanitized: raw logs are never committed; secrets are stripped; full transcripts stay local (only titles/summaries are shared).

This portal is one half of a reusable cockpit for AI-assisted build projects. The other half is a Markdown/JSON "brain" that agents read and update. Built to be shared so colleagues' agents can search it too.

cards.bodyHtml: This single-file HTML portal. No build step — open it, email it, host it anywhere. Content is data-driven from GOALS.md, PROGRESS.md and command-center/data/*.json.

CLAUDE.md → AGENTS.md → projects/agentforce-hackathon/AGENTS.md → GOALS.md gives any agent instant context; PROGRESS.md is the running log they maintain; harness mechanics live in command-center/HARNESS.md. For Salesforce work, the .agents/skills/ skills are authoritative.

The whole harness lives under command-center/; the active project under projects/. This cockpit was lifted from a prior project and repurposed by swapping data/portal.json + GOALS.md and changing one line (PROJECT_DIR) — never touching index.html.
Secrets (.env) and raw chat logs are gitignored; a commit-time hook blocks any key that slips into a diff; only sanitized summaries are published. Important here: the package is handed to customers.
